subtype: Teacher noticing a gap between effort and results [Observer]
passage: "Swati, stay back a minute?" "Did I do something wrong, Ma'am?" "No. The opposite. In class you explained why the river changes course better than anyone. Where did that come from?" "I just... see it. The water pushing on the soft bank." "But your written test has three lines." "I know." Swati looks at the floor. "I try. I write it again and again. It comes out wrong." "I believe you try. I've watched you." Urmila, the geography teacher, pulls a chair over. "Can I ask your parents to meet the counsellor about a screening? It checks how your brain handles reading and writing." "So I'm not lazy?" "Lazy people don't rewrite things again and again. And I won't ask you to read aloud without warning anymore. Deal?" "Deal."

qa.q: Which topic did Swati explain better than anyone in class?
Why does Swati ask, 'So I'm not lazy?'
qa.a: Swati seems worried that the short written work looks lazy, and hopes the teacher sees the effort.

qa.q: What choice does Urmila make instead of blaming Swati?
qa.a: Urmila suggests a screening through the counsellor and stops asking Swati to read aloud without warning.

qa.q: How might Swati's self-image change after this talk?
qa.a: Swati may stop feeling lazy and start seeing that the ideas are strong while writing is hard.

grounding: A teacher notices strong oral answers but weak written work, suggests screening, avoids reading aloud on the spot and values the student's ideas.

subtype: Teacher noticing a gap between effort and results [Observer]
passage: My name is Gopika, and I've taught maths for eleven years. I still think about Parveen, from two batches ago. She was the most careful student I had. Neat margins, every step written. And yet her answers were wrong in strange ways: 36 became 63, a plus sign read as a minus. At first I wrote "careless" in red. I'm not proud of that. Then I sat beside her during a test and watched. She was not careless. She was checking every line, lips moving, and still the digits slid. I stopped using red for those slips. I asked her family about a screening, and I started marking her method separately from her final number. Her method marks were among the best in the class. She stood a little straighter after that.

qa.q: What did Gopika write in red at first?
What does Gopika saying 'I'm not proud of that' show about how Gopika feels now?
qa.a: It shows regret; looking back, Gopika feels she misjudged Parveen's effort.

qa.q: What did Gopika change after watching Parveen during a test?
qa.a: Gopika stopped marking the slips in red, asked the family about a screening and marked Parveen's method separately.

qa.q: How might Parveen have felt when her method marks were among the best?
qa.a: She probably felt seen and proud, since her careful effort finally counted; she stood a little straighter.

grounding: A teacher sees careful effort with number errors, suggests screening and values the student's thinking, separating learning difference from lack of effort.
